results.claim: For p not dividing the base b, collision detection is exactly repeated-state detection on mismatch-only normalized prefix sums. Moreover, every collision has a witness containing at most p mismatching aligned positions, although its length may exceed p.
results.proof_sketch: Use the convention F(i,L)=sum_{t=0}^{L-1} s[i+t]b^{L-1-t} mod p. For displacement d define A_d(k)=sum_{t=0}^{k-1}(s[t]-s[t+d])b^{-(t+1)} mod p for 0<=k<=n-d. For r<e, multiplying A_d(e)-A_d(r) by b^e gives F(r,e-r)-F(r+d,e-r). Thus the two substrings collide exactly when A_d(r)=A_d(e) and the interval contains an actual mismatch. Let q_1<...<q_m be the mismatch positions between S[0..n-d) and S[d..n), and retain only B_0=0 and B_j=A_d(q_j+1). The state is constant between mismatches, so a true collision exists at displacement d iff two B_j are equal. A repeated pair B_a=B_c with a<c directly supplies unequal colliding substrings. If m>=p, the first p+1 states lie in F_p and two coincide; hence a collision with at most p mismatches exists. If m<p, every interval already has fewer than p mismatches.

results.claim: For p not dividing b, every collision-free input satisfies m_d<=p-1 at every displacement and M<=C(n,p):=sum_{d=1}^{n-1}min(n-d,p-1). Thus M>C(n,p) forces a collision, where C(n,p)=(p-1)(n-p/2) for p<=n and C(n,p)=n(n-1)/2 for p>=n.
results.proof_sketch: Let m_d be the Hamming distance between S[0..n-d) and S[d..n). The preceding repeated-state argument gives m_d<=p-1 on a collision-free input, while trivially m_d<=n-d. Also M=sum_d m_d=(n^2-sum_c n_c^2)/2 because each unequal unordered pair of positions contributes at its unique displacement. Summing gives the stated capacity C(n,p), so its violation forces some m_d>=p and hence a collision. Strict inequality is necessary: n=3, p=2, b=3, S=001 has M=C=2 but no collision. For p>=n, C equals the number of all position pairs, so this aggregate test is vacuous.

results.claim: In the word-RAM model with p=n^{O(1)}, there is an exact deterministic algorithm running in O(n log n+n+min{D,M,n min(n,p)}) time, where D is the number of distinct substring contents and M is the number of unequal unordered character-position pairs. Consequently the requested O(n log n) bound holds when p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n).
results.proof_sketch: First build suffix-array/LCP/RMQ support for constant-time LCE queries. For every displacement d, LCE jumps enumerate only the m_d mismatch positions. Update the normalized state from the preceding claim and record (d,state,boundary). Stop after p mismatches: p+1 states force a collision. Otherwise enumerate all mismatches. Sorting the records by (d,state) detects repeated states exactly. There are Q<=n+sum_d min(m_d,p) records. Since sum_d m_d=M=(n^2-sum_c n_c^2)/2 and sum_d min(n-d,p)=O(n min(n,p)), Q=O(n+min{M,n min(n,p)}). Word-sized keys permit constant-pass radix sorting. Independently, a compact suffix tree has one explicit or implicit locus per distinct substring and total edge-label length D. Traversing edge labels character-by-character computes every distinct substring fingerprint in O(D); radix-sort the (length,fingerprint) pairs. A duplicate pair is exactly a collision because each content occurs once. Compute D during preprocessing and choose the cheaper route. If S has period q, each length has at most q distinct contents, so D<=nq; in particular q=O(log n) gives O(n log n). All these algorithms have zero error probability.

results.claim: There is an infinite family of collision-free invertible-base instances with p=Theta(n), alphabet size at most n, D=Theta(n^2), M=Theta(n^2), and Theta(n^2) retained mismatch states. Hence both audited enumerative routes can require quadratic work even on valid NO instances; this is not a lower bound against arbitrary algorithms.
results.proof_sketch: For every prime p>=5, set n=p-2 and choose a primitive root b modulo p; its least positive representative lies in {2,...,p-2} and can be the alphabet size. Put a=floor(n/2), c=ceil(n/2), and S=0^a1^c. Every length-L content is 0^{L-k}1^k for a feasible k, with fingerprint H_k=1+b+...+b^{k-1}. If H_k=H_l for k!=l, then b^{k-l}=1 because b-1 is invertible. But 0<|k-l|<=n<p-1=ord_p(b), a contradiction. Thus there is no collision. The distinct contents are the a pure-zero words, c pure-one words, and ac crossing words, so D=n+ac; also M=ac. All m_d<p, so the mismatch route retains sum_d(m_d+1)=ac+n-1 states. Since ac=floor(n^2/4), both enumerations are quadratic.

results.claim: In the word-RAM model with p=n^{O(1)} and p not dividing b, every string with at most two runs has an exact O(n)-time collision test. For S=x^a y^c with x!=y and R=min(a,c), either x=y mod p gives a length-one collision, or a collision exists exactly when G_t:=1+b+...+b^{t-1}=0 mod p for some 1<=t<=R.
results.proof_sketch: A one-run string has only one distinct content at each length. For two runs, every distinct length-L content is x^{L-k}y^k for exactly one k in the integer interval K_L=[max(0,L-a),min(L,c)]. Its fingerprint is xG_L+(y-x)G_k. If x=y mod p, the distinct one-character contents collide. Otherwise, for k<l in K_L, the fingerprint difference is (y-x)(G_l-G_k)=(y-x)b^kG_{l-k}. Because p divides neither y-x nor b, this vanishes exactly when G_{l-k}=0. Every K_L has width at most R, so any collision supplies such a t<=R. Conversely, if G_t=0 for t<=R, both x^t and y^t occur and collide. Iterating G_0=0 and G_{t+1}=bG_t+1 through R performs the test in O(n) word operations. This nonenumerative decomposition therefore decides the quadratic family above in linear time.

results.claim: The target has a complete O(n log n) exact solution in the noninvertible case p divides b.
results.proof_sketch: With the most-significant-character-first convention, b=0 mod p makes every nonempty fingerprint equal to its last character modulo p. For an endpoint e, let R_e=s[e]s[e-1]...s[0]. For endpoints e<f having the same final-character residue, no collision between their substrings is possible exactly when R_e is a prefix of R_f; otherwise, if their longest common suffix has length t<e+1, the two length-(t+1) substrings ending at e and f are unequal but have the same fingerprint. Group endpoints by final-character residue and consider each group in increasing endpoint order. It suffices to test consecutive endpoints because the prefix relation is transitive. LCS queries are LCP queries in the reversed string and can be preprocessed in O(n log n), after which all tests take O(n). For the opposite polynomial-coefficient convention, reverse the roles of first and last characters.

results.claim: Collisions cannot occur at length L when b^L<=p, but checking only power-of-two lengths, only lexicographically adjacent contents, or relying on monotonicity in the length is insufficient.
results.proof_sketch: Distinct canonical base-b words of length L represent integers whose nonzero difference has magnitude at most b^L-1; if b^L<=p, that difference cannot be divisible by p. For the limitations, take b=2, p=5, and S=000101. The fingerprint arrays by length are: L=1: [0,0,0,1,0,1]; L=2: [0,0,1,2,1]; L=3: [0,1,2,0]; L=4: [1,2,0]; L=5: [2,0]; L=6: [0]. Repeated hashes at lengths 1 and 2 correspond only to equal contents. At length 3, 000 and 101 have integer values 0 and 5 and collide. Every other length is collision-free. Thus all power-of-two lengths 1,2,4 pass, and collision existence is not monotone. At length 3 the lexicographically ordered distinct contents have values 0,1,2,5, so the sole colliding pair is nonadjacent.

final_writeup:
Let b=Σ and encode symbols canonically as integers. I use F(i,L)=sum_{t=0}^{L-1}s[i+t]b^{L-1-t} mod p; reversing the input handles the opposite coefficient convention.

When p does not divide b, fix a displacement d and define A_d(k)=sum_{t<k}(s[t]-s[t+d])b^{-(t+1)} mod p. Then A_d(e)=A_d(r) is equivalent to equality of the fingerprints of S[r..e) and S[r+d..e+d). It is a genuine collision precisely when the interval contains a character mismatch. Because A_d is constant across aligned equal runs, only states immediately after mismatches matter. Thus collision detection is element distinctness in one field-state sequence per displacement, and p mismatches force a repeated state among p+1 boundaries.

Summing this per-displacement obstruction gives a stronger global certificate. If m_d is the aligned Hamming distance, collision-freeness requires m_d<=min(n-d,p-1). Therefore M=sum_d m_d=(n^2-sum_c n_c^2)/2 must not exceed C(n,p)=sum_d min(n-d,p-1). Here C=(p-1)(n-p/2) for p<=n and C=n(n-1)/2 for p>=n. Thus M>C certifies a collision, sharpening M>(n-1)(p-1). Equality is inconclusive, as S=001 with b=3,p=2 has M=C=2 and no collision; for p>=n the aggregate test is vacuous.

LCE jumps give an exact adaptive algorithm by enumerating at most p mismatches per displacement and sorting normalized states. A complementary compact-suffix-tree traversal enumerates distinct substring contents and sorts (length,fingerprint) keys. Together they run in O(n log n+n+min{D,M,n min(n,p)}) on a word RAM when p=n^{O(1)}. In particular, the requested O(n log n) bound holds when p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n), including strings of period O(log n).

The obstruction analysis also identifies a precise barrier to these routes. For every prime p>=5, take n=p-2, let the alphabet size b be a primitive root modulo p, and set S=0^{floor(n/2)}1^{ceil(n/2)}. A length-L substring is 0^{L-k}1^k and has hash 1+b+...+b^{k-1}. Distinct feasible k cannot collide because b has order p-1>n. Nevertheless M=floor(n^2/4), D=M+n, and the normalized route retains M+n-1 states. Thus both enumerations are quadratic on an infinite family of collision-free inputs with p=Theta(n). This is not a lower bound against a different algorithm.

A run decomposition confirms that this family itself is easy by a third route. More generally, let an invertible-base string have two runs, S=x^a y^c, and put R=min(a,c) and G_k=1+b+...+b^{k-1}. At length L its distinct contents are x^{L-k}y^k for k in [max(0,L-a),min(L,c)], with hashes xG_L+(y-x)G_k. If x=y mod p, there is a length-one collision. Otherwise two such contents collide exactly when G_{l-k}=0. The parameter intervals have width at most R, and x^t,y^t give the converse for every t<=R. Iterating G_{t+1}=bG_t+1 therefore decides every two-run instance exactly in O(n) time, including the quadratic-enumeration family.

If p divides b, every nonempty fingerprint reduces to its last character modulo p. Grouping endpoints by that residue and testing consecutive reversed-prefix relations gives a complete exact O(n log n) solution, with orientation reversed for the opposite convention.

Finally, fingerprints are injective at length L whenever b^L<=p. The exact instance S=000101 with b=2,p=5 collides only at length 3, between 000 and 101. It rules out checking only powers of two, assuming monotonicity in length, or comparing only lexicographically adjacent contents.

The general invertible-base case remains unresolved. The two-run decomposition yields no bound for arbitrary run counts, and neither it nor the mismatch and distinct-content routes supplies the requested worst-case algorithm. The explicit family limits only the two enumerative approaches analyzed here, not arbitrary algorithms.
